what: Why the naive slope is biased
title: Persistence meta-regression with ghreg
text: Write observed effect sizes true effects plus sampling error, δt=θt+et\delta_{t} = \theta_{t} + e_{t}, true effects related θ2=α+βθ1+η\theta_2 = \alpha + \beta\theta_1 + \eta. sampling errors correlated ρ\rho, least-squares slope δ2\delta_2 δ1\delta_1 converges β\beta plus ρVar(e1)Var(e2)Var(θ1)+Var(e1)⏟correlation-driven bias−βVar(e1)Var(θ1)+Var(e1)⏟attenuation bias. \underbrace{\frac{\rho\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(e_1)\mathrm{Var}(e_2)}}{\mathrm{Var}(\theta_1) + \mathrm{Var}(e_1)}}_{\text{correlation-driven bias}} \; - \; \underbrace{\frac{\beta\,\mathrm{Var}(e_1)}{\mathrm{Var}(\theta_1) + \mathrm{Var}(e_1)}}_{\text{attenuation bias}}. ρ=0\rho = 0 familiar attenuation measurement error predictor. difference means constant treatment effect, ρ\rho equals correlation outcome across time (test-retest reliability), typically well zero. ρ>β\rho > \beta two sampling variances similar, correlation term wins naive slope overstates persistence. standard errors--variables correction, assumes ρ=0\rho = 0, makes things worse.
